fullPassage: Traditionally, garbage is considered the detritus of consumer and industrial practices. It is the stuff that is no longer useful, that we no longer wish to have in our homes or personal spaces, that we want to throw away. Perhaps precisely due to the proliferation of trash in material space, it has arguably also become a resource — something that has value and can be sold on at a profit. Artists — most often at the leading edge of rethinking materiality, value, and beauty — are among the first social actors to have taken seriously the possibility of reusing trash to make new things. Taking the discarded objects of others as found materials, many artists work with trash in order to create new aesthetic objects while at the same time making a commentary on the place of trash in the social and cultural world.

Artists — most often at the leading edge of rethinking materiality, value, and beauty — are among the first social actors to have taken seriously the possibility of reusing trash ④<u>to make</u> new things. Taking the discarded objects of others as found materials, many artists work with trash in order to create new aesthetic objects while at the same time making a commentary on the place of trash in the social and cultural world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② to having → to have: wish + to부정사(to have). 전치사 to가 아니라 부정사 to이므로 동사원형 have.

❌ ① that: 'the stuff that is no longer useful' — 관계대명사 주격. 정상

✅ ② to having(오류): 'we no longer wish to have' — wish + to부정사. to 뒤 동사원형 have 필요. to having(동명사)은 부적절 ← 정답

❌ ③ become: 'has arguably also become a resource' — 현재완료의 과거분사. 정상

❌ ④ to make: 'reusing trash to make new things' — 목적의 to부정사. 정상
det.tip: wish/want + to부정사 = to + 동사원형(to have). 'be used to -ing'의 to와 혼동 금지.
